content.text: In 2022, we launched the free Planning Poker app to bring a user-friendly, convenient, and flexible native ecosystem experience to Azure DevOps Services users.

content.text: Welcome to Planning Poker for Azure DevOps!

app that facilitates agile team discussion aimed at reaching accurate and consensus-based estimations. Thanks to native Azure DevOps integration, teams can easily select game backlog, invite participants, view and edit issue details and comments during the poker session, and save their estimates for the selected fields.

attrs.alt: icon-feature-tools-blue-light.png

content.text: Planning Poker facilitates collaboration and discussion aimed at consensus-based estimations. It is a planning toolkit that supports interactive and async estimation.

attrs.alt: icon-feature-collaboration-blue-light.png

content.text: During the sessions, team members can voice their estimates unbiasedly and collaborate during group discussions to reach a consensus and achieve more accurate estimates.

attrs.alt: icon-feature-planning-poker-blue-light.png

content.text: The app also provides advanced features to help form a balance between the speed of the estimation process and expected accuracy, including multi-field estimation, custom estimation values, reference work items, and more.

The general idea of Planning Poker is that after a period of discussion, each participant chooses from their own deck the numbered card that represents their estimate of how much work is involved in the story under discussion.
All estimates are kept private until each participant has chosen a card. Then all estimates are revealed, and discussion can begin again.
This is all done inside the user’s Azure DevOps project.

is a collaborative estimation session where your Agile team estimates the effort and complexity of work items. Team members use a configurable card deck — Fibonacci, T-shirt sizes, S/M/L, or custom values — to submit their estimates. Each game assigns participants one of three roles:
(controls the session flow and approves final estimates),
(observes without voting). The game progresses through rounds of voting, discussion, and consensus for each item in the backlog.

Creating a game takes just a few steps: configure the session settings (name, estimation method, sync or async mode), assign participant roles, select work items by sprint, query, or manual addition, and launch. For more details, see the subpages below.

content.text: Use this guide to install the Planning Poker extension from the Azure DevOps Marketplace into your organization. This is a standard marketplace installation flow for Azure DevOps extensions and is intended for organization administrators or users with permission to manage extensions.
Planning Poker for Azure DevOps provides a native estimation experience inside Azure DevOps, including interactive estimation sessions, async estimation, and estimation directly from work item views.
